page: Amazon Web Services m6a.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.6 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs, which map to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per physical core. The instance does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core tests, and average in Geekbench single-core and single-threaded compression tests. However, due to the limited hardware footprint of 1 physical core, multi-core and parallelized workloads show significant limitations. Multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core scores, and Passmark CPU scores fall into the bottom 25% or bottom 10% categories. Memory subsystem performance is also constrained, with Passmark memory scores and uncached read/write bandwidth benchmarks ranking in the bottom 25% and bottom 10%.

Given its hardware profile, the m6a.large is positioned as an entry-level general-purpose resource. It offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation but do not demand high multi-threaded throughput or massive memory bandwidth. It is suitable for lightweight web serving, basic text processing, and small-scale application hosting. It is poorly suited for database operations, software compilation, ray tracing, or large-scale LLM inference, where its limited memory bandwidth and single-core physical bottleneck restrict throughput.
